Developed for NASA's Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge, ECHOES transforms forgotten space hardware into engaging learning experiences. By combining NASA mission data, interactive spacecraft archives, cinematic storytelling, educational quizzes, and an exploration game, we allow users to discover the remarkable achievements of machines left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

Each spacecraft tells its story, inviting visitors to explore its discoveries, understand its scientific contributions, and experience its journey through interactive challenges.

Our project addresses the challenge by making complex space science accessible, memorable, and exciting, particularly for younger generations.

By preserving these achievements through innovative digital experiences, we hope to inspire curiosity, encourage STEM education, and remind future explorers that even silent spacecraft have extraordinary stories worth telling.
details:
ECHOES — The Museum of Unfinished Journeys

Project Overview

ECHOES is an immersive, web-based educational platform developed for NASA's Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge. Our project transforms the stories of abandoned and inactive spacecraft into interactive learning experiences, combining scientific accuracy, creative storytelling, and engaging digital exploration.

Spacecraft that have completed their missions are often remembered for their final moments rather than the extraordinary scientific discoveries they made possible. ECHOES aims to change that by giving these machines a digital voice and ensuring their contributions continue inspiring future generations.

How Does ECHOES Work?

ECHOES invites users to explore a digital museum dedicated to spacecraft left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

Our platform includes several interactive experiences:

  • Interactive Spacecraft Archive: Visitors discover real NASA missions through detailed scientific information, mission histories, and imaginative first-person stories.
  • Space Exploration Game: Players become SCOUT-07, an exploration drone traveling through different environments to discover abandoned space hardware, solve science challenges, and uncover mission histories.
  • Mission Atlas: An interactive experience that introduces visitors to the worlds where spacecraft completed their journeys.
  • Scientific Data Visualizations: Users compare planned mission durations with actual achievements, demonstrating how spacecraft exceeded expectations.
  • Mission Control: Educational quizzes allow students to test their understanding of NASA missions and receive explanations.
  • Signal Wall: Visitors can write personal messages to spacecraft, creating an emotional connection with the history of space exploration.

The platform integrates information from official NASA mission resources, including NASA Science and the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA). Scientific facts are distinguished from fictional storytelling and illustrative simulations.

Technology and Development

ECHOES was developed as a browser-based interactive experience using web technologies, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and deployed through Netlify.

The project combines frontend development, interactive interface design, animations, educational game mechanics, and NASA mission research.

AI-assisted tools supported aspects of prototyping, programming, creative writing, and design development. Our approach combines technology with human-directed creativity and research to produce an accessible educational experience.

The platform is designed to operate through a web browser without requiring specialized hardware or software installation.

Creativity and Innovation

What distinguishes ECHOES is its combination of scientific education and emotional storytelling.

Rather than presenting spacecraft as static museum exhibits, we allow visitors to discover their scientific contributions through imagined narratives, interactive challenges, and exploration.

Our central creative question is:

What if the machines we left behind could tell us everything they discovered?

By humanizing the stories of robotic explorers while preserving the distinction between verified science and fiction, ECHOES creates a memorable connection between students and space exploration.

Our companion game extends this concept by turning passive reading into active discovery.

Intended Impact and Benefits

ECHOES is designed primarily for school-age students, young space enthusiasts, educators, and curious learners.

Our goals are to:

  • Make NASA's scientific achievements more accessible and understandable.
  • Encourage interest in STEM subjects and space exploration.
  • Promote curiosity, discovery, and independent learning.
  • Preserve awareness of historically significant space missions.
  • Demonstrate how interactive technology can transform science communication.

By presenting authentic scientific information through engaging digital experiences, we aim to help students connect with space science in a more meaningful way.

Design Considerations and Feasibility

Throughout development, our team prioritized scientific accuracy, creativity, accessibility, educational value, and user experience.

We considered how to make complex mission information understandable without oversimplifying the science, how to distinguish fictional narratives from NASA facts, and how to maintain an engaging experience for different audiences.

The project demonstrates a practical approach to digital science education: an accessible website that can be explored by students from virtually anywhere with an internet connection.

Conclusion

ECHOES is more than a digital archive. It is an invitation to rediscover humanity's achievements through the machines that made them possible.

Our project reflects the belief that a spacecraft does not become insignificant when its mission ends. Its discoveries remain part of humanity's scientific legacy.

Through interactive storytelling, verified NASA information, and educational gameplay, ECHOES seeks to transform abandoned space hardware into lasting sources of knowledge, inspiration, and wonder.

Because every mission has an ending, but every discovery deserves to live on.
